newsitem.title: USA: Mass. politicos battle over "Big Dig" funds - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass. politicos battle over "Big Dig" funds - paper.

text.p: An unreleased legislative study could split the western portion of the Massachusetts Turnpike roadway from the eastern portion, with each portion paying for its own outstanding debt and the eastern portion picking up some of the tab for the Third Harbor/Central Artery project, the Boston Herald reported Thursday.

The section east of Route 128 would include the Central Artery, also known as the "Big Dig," and all three tunnels which run underneath Boston Harbor, according to the newspaper. Revenue and traffic projections in the study through the year 2020 look at the prospect of regular toll hikes on the harbor crossings and the possibility of future toll hikes on the eastern section of the roadway.

The study, ordered by the Legislature last year was designed to look at how MassPike and the Massachusetts Port Authority, which operates Logan Airport, could help pay the state's share of the $10.4 billion project.

The state's own finance plan shows that Massachusetts share of the Big Dig, once expected to be 14 percent could mushroom to 35 percent by the project's 2004 completion date because of federal funding cuts.
MassPike bonds carry a A-plus rating from Standard & Poors Corp, and an A1 from Moody's Investors Service. MassPort bonds are rated AA by S&P and Moody's.
Both MassPort and MassPike officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
